newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil slips, all eyes on IPE expiry.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil slips, all eyes on IPE expiry.

text.p: NWE gas oil prices retreated in sympathy with lower futures but trade was virtually at a standstill in the runup to the expiry of the November futures contract, traders said.
IPE November futures expired 50 cents down at $220 a tonne and the December contract slipped $1.75 to $210 as the relatively calm end of the November contract took some fizz out of the market.
Around 500,000 tonnes or more is expected to be delivered into the contract and whether this material can then be sold outside the region is dominating sentiment.
"Today is very quiet because everyone is looking at IPE expiry, one trader said.

"It looks to me that there will be a huge delivery into the screen of an estimated 650,000, maybe 700,000 tonnes, but we will only know that for sure in a couple of hours' time. That is ruling the market and so trading came to a standstill."

A barge of refinery grade prompt heating oil sold at Nov IPE -$0.50/0.75. One trader heard refinery grade material offered at Dec +$10 prompt with low sulphur at Dec +$16/17. Prompt heating oil cargoes were around Dec +$8.50/11.
